enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 1–3 establish the Act and its relationship with the Indian Contract Act; sections 4–8 define partnership and distinguish partnership from status, prescribe tests for existence, partnership at will and particular partnership; sections 9–17 regulate general duties and mutual rights of partners, property, application of profits and losses and contractual variation.

Definition: Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.

Ingredients:
1. Agreement between persons.
2. Agreement to share profits of a business.
3. Business carried on by all or any acting for all, establishing mutual agency.
4. Apply sections 5–8 to determine whether partnership exists and whether it is at will or particular.
5. Apply the mutual duties and rights in sections 9–17.
examples: A and B agree to carry on a business, share its profits and allow each to act for both; the section 4 definition and section 6 factual test determine whether a partnership exists.
problemApplication: Apply sections 1–17: identify the statutory relationship or transaction, test each ingredient, consider exceptions or limitations, and conclude.
keyTakeaways: Sections 1–3 establish the Act and its relationship with the Indian Contract Act; sections 4–8 define partnership and distinguish partnership from status, prescribe tests for existence, partnership at will and particular partnership; sections 9–17 regulate general duties and mutual rights of partners, property, application of profits and losses and contractual variation.
Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
